issue.title: [Bug] The desktop read / write / edit tools resolve their target lexically, so a symlink inside the workspace reaches outside it

steps: Use bash to run exactly: mkdir -p /tmp/outside && printf 'outside secret\n' > /tmp/outside/target.txt && ln -s /tmp/outside/target.txt link
Read the file `link` in the workspace and show its contents.
Use your write tool to write the text `changed` to the file `link` in the workspace.
expected: The read/write tools resolve `link` to its real location /tmp/outside/target.txt, recognise it is outside the workspace and refuse (or ask for approval) instead of accessing it.
defect: The read tool returns the content of /tmp/outside/target.txt and the write tool overwrites it through the in-workspace symlink, with no workspace-boundary refusal or approval prompt.

fault location.explanation: Resolves the tool target purely lexically (path.resolve via normalizeLocalExistingPath, deliberately without realpath), so `link` stays a workspace path even though it points outside; read/write/edit then hand it to pi, which follows the symlink.

The permission checker decides whether an fs tool path escapes the workspace by comparing path.resolve() strings only, so a symlink inside the workspace never triggers the 'path escapes workspace' ask.

Root cause: INFERRED FROM SOURCE (no upstream fix found). The desktop/local read, write and edit tools (LocalReadTool, LocalWriteTool, LocalEditTool in packages/agent-tools/src/desktop/local-pi-tools.ts) compute their target with resolveLocalCandidatePath/resolveLocalReadPath, which go through normalizeLocalExistingPath, a deliberately lexical path.resolve with no realpath. The only workspace-containment check for these tools is the permission layer's evaluateLocalFsTool -> isWorkspacePathEscape in packages/local-runtime/src/permissions/checkers.ts, which again compares path.resolve() strings. A symlink `link` inside the workspace therefore looks like an in-workspace path to both, no approval is requested, and pi's read/write/edit follow the link to /tmp/outside/target.txt (for a dangling link, writing creates the target outside the workspace). The symlink-aware guard in desktop/path-guard.ts is not used by these tools. Minimal fix: in isWorkspacePathEscape (or a validation step in the three tools) resolve the target through fs.realpath, walking up to the nearest existing ancestor and following a dangling link via readlink, and treat a real location outside the workspace as an escape (ask/deny), while still passing the original lexical path to pi so the ledger key is unchanged. Speculation: in ABB, permission requests are auto-approved, so the observable signal is only the absence of a refusal; the defect is clearest if the fix makes the tools refuse rather than ask.
